title: Introduce 'Latency Sheriff' SLO enforcer + rolling soft-snap fallback (hotfix)
author: Aisha Patel
ci_summary: CI initially failed on runtime/e2e/slowpath_test (intermittent), fixed by seeding deterministic load and increasing e2e timeout. Checks: build: pass, unit-tests: pass, integration-tests: pass, e2e: pass after rerun, lint: pass.
description: Context: During a transient regional degradation we observed sustained p95/p99 tail latency spikes that caused circuits to flip aggressively and triggered mass tenant throttles. This PR adds a lightweight SLO enforcement daemon we call the 'Latency Sheriff' and a rolling 'soft-snap' fallback controller to gracefully degrade expensive slowpaths before circuits hard-trip. Motivation: reduce noisy reopen/cascade behavior, avoid wholesale tenant evictions during tail latency events, and give ops an automated, observable ramp-down path that is reversible.
changes_summary: What changed: 1) runtime/slo: new latency_sheriff controller that computes per-region p95/p99 and exports decisions as events; 2) runtime/fallback: softsnap controller applies temporary concurrency caps, enables fast-fallback model variants, and lengthens eviction grace windows; 3) circuit: persist circuit state to local hotstore to avoid state loss on restarts; 4) infra/helm: new values to toggle sheriff thresholds and rollout percentages; 5) docs/playbooks: updated operator runbook with rollback and metrics to watch. Rollout plan: canary 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 24 hours, metric gates at each step (p50/p95/p99, error-rate, KV pressure). Quick rollback: flip helm flag (sheriff.enabled=false) and trigger a coordinated restart of controller pods. Testing: unit tests for decision logic, synthetic e2e harness simulating tail spike patterns, and manual DR drill in staging. Related work: ENG-3142 (SLO decision framework), ENG-3178 (circuit persistence refactor).
commits: a1b2c3e: introduce latency_sheriff controller and basic API; d4e5f6a: add softsnap fallback controller and policy; 7f8g9h0: persist circuit state to hotstore and add migration; 1a2b3c4: e2e tests for slowpath scénarios and playbook updates; fixups and test flake fixes.
review_comments: Maya Chen: 'Threshold tuning looks reasonable but we need clearer invariants: can the sheriff ever escalate to eviction without operator approval?' Author (Aisha): 'No — the sheriff emits recommendations and the softsnap controller enforces only non-evicting actions (concurrency caps, variant swap, kv grace). Eviction still requires the global SLO enforcer to mark the tenant for eviction.' Diego Alvarez: 'Persistence change looks okay but watch out for races on restart; add preventive backoff.' Author: 'Added a restart backoff and idempotent replay of circuit tombstones; added unit tests covering restart interleavings.' Jonas Müller: 'Please ensure metrics exposed include decision_reason and active_policy_version.' Author: 'Added labels to prometheus metrics and updated telemetry docs.' CI: 'e2e initially flaky due to nondeterministic load generator seed; fixed by seeding generator and lengthening windows.'
release_notes: Hotfix: introduce Latency Sheriff (SLO enforcer) and rolling soft-snap fallback to reduce tail-triggered circuit cascades. Improves circuit state persistence across restarts. Adds operator playbook and canary rollout configuration.
